checks: Both decoders read raw, fast-clear and single-stored-texel encodings across 45 formats, including floating point, signed colors, RGB10A2, R11G11B10_FLOAT and A8.
Eighteen eight-bit component formats use compressed 32- and 64-byte chunks. Tested independent channels, green-channel decorrelation, and all 16 combinations of solid and noisy sectors.

120,960 cross-codec comparisons used low-amplitude noise, gradients, isolated impulses and byte wraparound. Both encode/decode directions matched for all three prediction window sizes and all three tested dimension values, including cross-sector width inheritance.
Clear/raw checks covered eight swizzles (0 through 28, step 4), three block sizes, two channel configurations and dimension values 0, 3 and 4.
remaining: Compressed deltas in formats with wider components and additional swizzles. Encoding can fall back to hardware-valid raw blocks.
reproduce: python build.py xg; run build/xg-provider/xg-dcc.exe alongside the supplied xg_xs.dll renamed to xg_reference.dll and its xmem dependency. The regular xg-provider suite embeds two reference encodings and needs no Xbox binaries.
